diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber's aggregation router has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold; the recorded CPU, memory, and temperature values are stale last-known values rather than evidence of current reachability.
evidence: The trigger is a stale router heartbeat of 7.4 hours, which is in the danger range above 4 hours.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has healthy CPU, memory, and temperature, and all eight PONs are reported healthy, so this is not an OLT or PON infrastructure failure.
The subscriber ONU is online with a responding live probe, normal RX power of -20.61 dBm, normal TX power of 2.40 dBm, stable distance, and healthy bias current history.
All visible peers on EPON0/2 are online and responding, excluding a shared splitter or port failure.
The optical telemetry shows no RX decline, TX instability, distance change, or laser-bias rise.
The session count is one in 24 hours with a duration near the network mean, so there is no session flapping or RADIUS presentation fault.
RADIUS records are present and CRM-consistent, and the expected customer VLAN 1062 is active, excluding missing authentication and VLAN 46 provisioning faults.
The only current abnormality is the router heartbeat timeout, so the fault is scoped to the router.

remediation.action: Check reachability and management access to router TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01, including ping, RouterOS/API, and SNMP. Inspect power, uplinks, and system logs; restore or reboot the router if it is actually unreachable. If the router is reachable, repair the heartbeat/monitoring agent and verify fresh check-ins. Do not dispatch for an EPON, fibre, splitter, OLT, VLAN, or RADIUS fault.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
